# Executive summary

R educators can choose among several tools for interactive teaching, but finding a suitable tutorial and checking that it still works remains difficult. Lessons use different formats and describe their requirements inconsistently. An instructor comparing them often has to inspect each repository, check its dependencies, and determine whether anyone still maintains it.

**tutorialverse will help instructors find R tutorials, understand their requirements, and see when they were last checked and reviewed.** We will build an R package with adapters that connect existing tutorial engines to a common checking interface. Tutorial descriptions and validation reports will use a shared format. A searchable registry will index tutorials in their original repositories, with a community process for reviewing submissions and handling outdated entries.

The 12-month project will initially support learnr, learnr2, and Quarto Live, and index Carpentries-style materials with stated limits on automated checks. Four small example tutorials will test the adapters across teaching contexts. Community feedback helped focus this proposal on shared metadata and checks. Browser execution and static hosting will use existing tools.
